Alexandros Kaminas

PhD researcher, TRÊS, University of Groningen

Modelling complex systems.

I build mathematical and computational models of systems whose behaviour emerges from interaction, feedback and chance: communities of species, evolving populations, and the organisations and economies that depend on them.

Explore the island below to find my projects, methods, publications and teaching: the sea leads to marine work, the island to ecology and evolution, the three figures to social and economic systems, and each house to a page.

Core expertise

Mechanistic models of interacting components: dynamical systems, stochastic simulation, population and trait-based models, and networks of interactions. The question is always how structure and randomness at one level produce behaviour at another.

Primary domain

Ecology and evolution. My doctoral research at the University of Groningen models how isolation and limited immigration reshape community assembly, diversification and extinction, with ecological and evolutionary change coupled.

Interdisciplinary applications

Sustainability and socioeconomic systems, where I apply the same systems reasoning to organisations and institutions: a 2026 paper on organisational commitment to sustainability, and policy and reporting work with SDSN Youth Greece and the University of Athens.

How the models are built

The subject changes from project to project; the toolkit does not. Models are formulated mechanistically, studied by stochastic simulation and dynamical-systems analysis, and confronted with data using statistical methods. Simulation engines in C++, analysis and visualisation in R and Python.

  • Eco-evolutionary models
  • Stochastic simulation
  • Dynamical systems & transitions
  • Interaction networks
  • Trait-space & functional diversity
  • Statistical modelling
  • Spatial analysis
  • Data visualisation
